diagrams.title: Launching a VAR Motion That Pays
diagrams.subtitle: License as entry ticket, services as the profit layer
diagrams.caption: Operators sequence a VAR motion from proven direct sales through published implementation ballparks, a full license stack, transparent quoting and go-live tracking.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Step order follows the operator gates in Chapter Q1. No durations or margins are added beyond those stated by the cited practitioners.
diagrams.note: Sources: Phil Morettini [L1YsH5QkIus @ 00:02:18]; Channel Marketing Academy [vLO0gA3TgxE @ 00:01:38]; Stuart Sutton [yasPH-UlTQo @ 00:08:10]; Ben Fox of TC2 via Staying Connected [BJPNVL1CIiM @ 00:04:10]; Summer Zaldivar [4qYKEjVIAjc @ 00:00:36].

stages.label: Prove direct sales first
stages.detail: Phil Morettini: no one can sell your product if you cannot, and VARs will not create demand for a vendor.

stages.label: Publish implementation ballparks
stages.detail: Entry, medium and heavy ballparks such as a month and a half, six months and two years; a $50,000 surprise on a $5,000 buyer embarrasses the VAR.

stages.label: Stack setup, minimum and usage fees
stages.detail: Stuart Sutton layers setup fees, monthly minimums, usage pricing and per-hour customization; the minimum covers subscribers whose usage falls below the cost of cutting an invoice.

stages.label: Break out markup and tax lines
stages.detail: Ben Fox has seen a 60 percent OEM discount passed through as 58 percent, and customs and import fees disguised as taxes.

stages.label: Track go-live and active users
stages.detail: Summer Zaldivar: of 20 at-risk high-volume customers, eight were remediated via premier support, saving over 250,000 and lifting renewal rate by 5 percent.

diagrams.title: Microsoft CSP Commitment Ladder
diagrams.subtitle: Direct-bill costs narrowing down to the indirect floor
diagrams.caption: Direct bill now demands a $1 million trailing revenue bar, a billing marketplace and a paid support plan, while indirect resellers stay authorized on $1,000 a year.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Stages are ordered by dollar commitment, not by customer conversion. Conversion text quotes practitioner commentary and adds no computed rates.
diagrams.note: Sources: Jeff Edwards and Scott May of Stratos Cloud Alliance [rV-Q2IVur6I @ 00:03:12, 00:08:45, 00:12:14]; Pax8 APAC [Xywyds1IfvM @ 00:05:09]; David Bujaider of Manage Protect [Je2jbg9tm0Q @ 00:09:37].

stages.label: Direct-bill CSP revenue bar
stages.conversion: Up from $300,000; Pax8 expects upwards of two-thirds of direct partners to move indirect
stages.detail: Also requires a solutions partner designation and a heavier security score.

stages.label: Direct-bill billing marketplace build
stages.detail: Scott May: direct-bill partners build and run the transacting marketplace with their own people and money.

stages.label: Premier support plan spend
stages.conversion: Basic plan at least 15k if not more
stages.detail: A premier or advanced support plan becomes mandatory for direct bill.

stages.label: Indirect rebate threshold
stages.conversion: Stratos: indirect resellers earn the exact same back-end incentives as direct sellers

stages.label: Indirect authorization floor
stages.conversion: Minimum to stay an authorized CSP
stages.detail: Confirm the Partner Center legal entity, address and current contact, then have a global admin accept the MPA.

diagrams.title: From Boxes to Services
diagrams.subtitle: Partner revenue mix and a UK partner's services delivery split
diagrams.caption: Hardware is down to 16 percent of partner revenue, and a large UK services-led partner outsources 60 percent of services delivery to 300+ providers.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Two percentage waterfalls share one chart, each starting from a 100 percent base implied by the reported shares. Deduction values are magnitudes; kind sets direction.
diagrams.note: Sources: Jay McBain of Canalys via Channel Partners Events [SwebwmaZR2I @ 00:02:55]; Sophia of TD SYNNEX [2qmTwyQCa_o @ 00:02:25, 00:02:45].

diagrams.title: Reseller Margin Bands in Practice
diagrams.subtitle: Where operators set, and dispute, partner economics
diagrams.caption: Ted Finch's tier template runs 10/20/30 percent, Luasai puts the combined distributor and VAR take at 5 to 10 percent, and Viktor's guest says 20 to 30 percent usually is not enough.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Single stated values repeat across min, max and typical. For stated ranges without a typical figure, typical equals the stated lower bound.
diagrams.note: Sources: Ted Finch tier template (Chapter Q2 summary); Luasai [9ijiF4Aas8o @ 00:14:38]; Viktor from Sales guest [6Z4v3jibmMw @ 00:07:14].

bars.label: Band called insufficient
bars.display: 20-30% usually is not going to be enough (Viktor's guest)

diagrams.title: Channel Partner Private Offer Readiness
diagrams.subtitle: Four gates before an AWS CPPO goes to the buyer
diagrams.caption: AWS walks resellers through listing eligibility, resale authorization, buyer targeting and cash forecasting before a CPPO is sent.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Gate order mirrors the Chapter Q5 operator gates. Payment timing uses only the 25-day average lag and the 7th-10th disbursement window reported by AWS.
diagrams.note: Sources: Amazon Web Services [PkznZxwv3eg @ 00:01:43, 00:08:13, 00:12:57]; Amazon Web Services [pOUxsKDRzvM @ 00:02:26]; Amazon Web Services [vKzo7FINzss @ 00:02:42].

nodes.question: Does the ISV have a paid listing, and are you a registered AWS Marketplace seller?
nodes.fail_action: Do not quote; BYOL and free products are excluded from CPPO.

nodes.question: Have you accepted the seller's reseller agreement, and is the resale authorization inside its validity window?
nodes.fail_action: Hold the offer build; push the ISV for a recurring authorization instead of a one-time discount.

nodes.question: Will the buyer receive both the private offer link and the targeted AWS account ID?
nodes.fail_action: Put the account ID next to the link in the offer email; the buyer must be logged into that exact account.

nodes.question: Does the forecast pad for the 25-day average payment lag and any net 30, 45 or 60 terms?
nodes.pass_next: Send the offer; cash lands between the 7th and 10th of the month after invoicing.
nodes.fail_action: Pad the revenue forecast before committing numbers.

diagrams.title: Public Sector Reseller Desk
diagrams.subtitle: Contract vehicles at the center, risk controls on every spoke
diagrams.caption: Public sector resellers win on contract vehicles, not relationships, and pair schedule and marketplace roles with pricing and vendor-risk controls.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Roles are grouped from the Chapter Q11 mechanics; no practitioner stated a headcount, so none is given.
diagrams.note: Sources: Clovity [fwAcWt5Q8oA @ 00:06:37]; GSA trainer [NVfgGOTkm4Q @ 00:02:34, 00:10:16]; How To Sell To & Win Federal Government Contracts [p3DsAuDE32c @ 00:12:11]; AWS Public Sector [F4gkR0s1Blw @ 00:02:10]; SecureOps with Ayden Connor [fOUGaSjlTBY @ 00:00:17]; Leegality [DeATzRK3azc @ 00:03:22].

center.focus: Efficiency through contract vehicles; GSA schedule buys run about 10 days versus about 270 on the open market

spokes.kpi: 0.75% IFF reported under the correct SIN; $25,000 annual sales minimum; avoid the 60%+ zero-sales group
1-60 month terms, up to 60 payments, naso or bid terms replacing commercial terms
No commercial quote below the GSA rate; CALC benchmarking; counteroffer reply by close of business tomorrow
Bank-detail changes confirmed on a known number; every cancellation window tracked after a 75 percent remaining-contract liability case

diagrams.title: Where a $100 Private Offer Lands
diagrams.subtitle: AWS worked example of discount, listing fee and ISV net
diagrams.total_range: $100 list price to $72 ISV net revenue
diagrams.caption: A 20 percent private offer discount takes a $100 list to $80, and a 10 percent listing fee leaves the ISV $72.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The list price bucket is the reference total; the other three buckets decompose it. The $8 listing fee is 10 percent of the $80 customer price, as stated in the example.
diagrams.note: Source: Amazon Web Services worked example [qWl-wamuA-Q @ 00:10:25].

buckets.notes: Starting list price in the AWS example

buckets.label: Private offer discount
buckets.notes: 20 percent discount; AWS charges the customer $80

buckets.label: AWS listing fee
buckets.notes: 10 percent listing fee on the $80 price

diagrams.title: Audit Defense and Negotiation Roadmap
diagrams.subtitle: Leverage exists before signature
diagrams.caption: Lock auditor terms, close license gaps, harden contract escalators and negotiate with a credible walk-away.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Weekly grouping is a sequencing frame only; practitioners cited 30-day respond and settle deadlines but no weekly schedule.
diagrams.note: Sources: SAMexpert TV [7shzxv1SUFc @ 00:10:22, 00:18:31, 00:54:49, 01:09:04, 01:15:49]; SAMexpert TV [S-D4c7b8-94 @ 00:14:57]; Virtualization Options LLC [xP4R2F8hbBw @ 00:06:54]; Virtualization Options LLC [fTqBORy9ePo @ 00:03:00, 00:05:39]; Heartland Business Systems [jqaG0NHe-0c @ 00:00:57].

weeks.title: Lock auditor kickoff terms
weeks.deliverable: Direct NDA signed with the auditor; nothing handed over, not even the org structure

weeks.title: Close compliance gaps
weeks.deliverable: Per-user SPLA counts include everyone authorized through VNC, Guacamole or TeamViewer
weeks.gate: Non-compliance below 5 percent, avoiding licenses at 125 percent of the discounted price list plus $27k-$40k in audit fees

weeks.title: Harden contract terms
weeks.deliverable: 3-5 percent annual escalator cap against 15-25 percent uncapped drift over three years
weeks.gate: Costed exit pilot complete, with discount sequenced last

weeks.title: Negotiate or switch partner
weeks.deliverable: Microsoft talks timed to its June year-end; midterm CSP transfer tool ready if the partner offers no renewal help
weeks.gate: Walk-away position credible to the vendor
